subject: sentences
title: Real or make-believe?
about: Telling things that could really happen (a dog digs in the yard) from make-believe (a dog drives a bus to the moon), and telling a story book from a book that gives facts. NC RL.1.5 asks first graders to explain the big differences between books that tell stories and books that give information.
tip: Ask him how he knows: could you see it happen in our yard, or only in a story?

cards.q: Which one could a real dog do?
wrong: drive a bus to the moon
cards.note: Dogs really dig. Driving a bus and reading are make-believe for a dog.

cards.q: Which one could a real cat do?
cards.note: Cats really nap in the sun. The other two could only happen in a story.

cards.q: Which one could a real boy do?
cards.note: You can ride a bike. No one can ride a cloud or a rainbow.

cards.q: Which one could a real hen do?
cards.note: Hens really lay eggs. Talking on a phone and driving are make-believe for a hen.

cards.q: Which one really happens in the sky?
cards.note: Rain really comes from clouds. Candy rain and singing clouds are make-believe.
Fish cannot talk. That only happens in a story.
Trees cannot walk. Their roots hold them in the ground.
A cow cannot get to the moon. That is make-believe, like in the rhyme.
Frogs hop and sit on logs. A frog driving a car is pretend.
Bears really sleep all winter and eat fish. Baking pies is make-believe.
A book about how bees make honey gives information. Bees cannot sing or go to school, so those are stories.

wrong: a frog with a magic hat
cards.note: All about frogs gives real information. Flying frogs and magic hats are a story.

cards.q: Which seed book gives true facts?
cards.note: How a seed grows is information. A talking seed is make-believe.

cards.q: Which pig book is a story?
cards.note: A pig who talks is make-believe, so that book is a story. The other two tell facts.
Dragons are make-believe, so that is a story book. Lizards and snakes are real.
Trucks do not fly. A flying truck is a story. The other two are information books.
